newsitem.title: USA: White House pushes lower defense spending for FY97.
newsitem.headline: White House pushes lower defense spending for FY97.

text.p: White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta told reporters on Monday that he will urge Congress to cut its proposed fiscal year 1997 defense appropriation of $2.45 billion to pay for higher spending on education.
Panetta spoke as he entered a closed meeting with House of Representatives and Senate Appropriations Committee leaders.

"It is important to make this package work that defense be part of the package under consideration. That's the best way to put this together," he said when asked if he would seek lower defense spending levels.
The White House has argued that Congress is working toward a defense level of about $11 billion more than is necessary.
Democrats have proposed an increase in education and other programs worth about $3.1 billion.

Panetta met with the Democratic and Republican committee leaders to discuss an overall spending figure for domestic and defense programs which could be passed by Congress before the October 1 start of the new fiscal year.
"Our concern is always to ensure that the investments we care about, particularly education, are funded at levels to preserve the commitment," he said.
